stories.headline: Federal agents raid Ilhan Omar's DC home amid immigration fraud investigation
stories.note: Homeland Security agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home before dawn Monday as part of a criminal fraud probe into her immigration paperwork.
body: Federal agents from Homeland Security Investigations searched the Washington, D.C., home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, the Minnesota Democrat, early Monday morning, according to a source who spoke with Fox News Digital. Agents in HSI jackets were seen outside the house, and the operation began around 6 a.m.

Two sources close to the case told Fox the search is tied to a criminal fraud investigation into Omar's immigration paperwork, which her late father filled out when she was a child. HSI and the Department of Homeland Security led the operation, with the Justice Department also involved.

A DOJ spokesperson confirmed that HSI carried out a search warrant secured by the department and approved by a judge, calling it part of "an ongoing federal investigation," and later said the probe is criminal. Border czar Tom Homan had said back in mid-September that Omar was the subject of a criminal investigation.

Omar has also faced months of questions about her financial disclosures. In 2024 she reported her husband held between $6 million and $30 million in assets, but her 2025 report put the couple's shared assets at no more than $125,000, with debts that could leave them with a negative net worth. She has repeatedly declined to explain the change.

Why it matters: A federal search of a sitting Democratic congresswoman's home is a major blow to one of the party's best-known progressives, and it keeps questions about her background and finances in the headlines three weeks before the midterms. Fox notes the story is still developing.

stories.headline: Trump announces immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
stories.note: Trump announced Russia and Ukraine have both agreed to stop hitting each other's energy infrastructure, a move aimed at easing diesel and fuel prices for Americans.
body: President Trump announced Sunday that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to an immediate halt to attacks on each other's energy infrastructure, after weeks of strikes on oil refineries and power plants. "Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" he wrote on Truth Social.

Trump has been pressing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop striking Russian refineries, arguing the attacks have squeezed global diesel supplies and pushed up fuel costs for American farmers, truckers and businesses.

The announcement follows a deal Trump struck with Vladimir Putin, announced Friday, under which Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, with more shipments expected in November and beyond. Treasury approved temporary sanctions relief to make it happen. Zelenskyy criticized that deal as a concession that could help fund Russia's war, and on Saturday Trump said Ukraine should get a leader "who can make a deal."

Zelenskyy has said Ukraine would stop hitting Russian refineries if Moscow stopped targeting Ukraine's power plants. Fox notes Trump announced a similar energy ceasefire in September that Moscow never publicly confirmed, and it's not yet clear how this one will be monitored or enforced. The White House and both embassies hadn't responded to requests for comment.

Why it matters: If it holds, the deal gives Trump a diplomatic win and a direct pitch to voters on lower diesel and gas prices heading into the midterms, an issue that has been weighing on Republicans.

stories.headline: Democrats see new chances to flip red states — but a $400M GOP spending advantage could derail their plans
stories.note: Republicans and their allies have outspent Democrats by $400 million this cycle, and Democratic groups are openly admitting they can't keep up.
body: With about three weeks until Election Day, Republican campaigns, party committees and allied groups have outspent their Democratic counterparts by $400 million this cycle, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact.

Democrats are being forced into tough choices about where to spend. Lauren French of the Schumer-aligned Senate Majority PAC told Fox plainly, "We are being outspent by the Republicans. That's just a fact." New Hampshire Democratic Senate nominee Chris Pappas told supporters he's being outspent 3-to-1 after a pro-Trump PAC reserved $10 million in ads there.

An anonymous veteran Democratic operative told Fox there isn't enough money to defend the toss-up states and also go on offense in red-leaning ones. On the House side, a DCCC memo to donors warned that MAGA Inc. and Trump-aligned super PAC money is flooding districts in amounts Democrats can't match, and asked for another $17 million by Oct. 22.

The GOP edge comes from heavy spending by the Senate Leadership Fund, Trump-allied MAGA Inc. and a super PAC funded by Elon Musk. A Senate Leadership Fund spokesman credited Leader John Thune for building a financial advantage he said neither party has had before. Fox notes Democrats still see openings in races like Alaska, Iowa, Ohio and Texas, and that Republicans face midterm history, inflation and Trump's approval ratings as headwinds.
Why it matters: GOP strategist Jesse Hunt said the money is a big reason many Republican candidates are keeping their races close, and it could be the deciding factor in holding the House and Senate.

stories.headline: Blue-state governor's race defies expectations as Republican closes in: Power Rankings
stories.note: Fox News Power Rankings moved Oregon's governor race toward the GOP as Republican Christine Drazan pulls within the margin of error against Democratic Gov. Tina Kotek.
body: Fox News Power Rankings shifted Oregon's governor race from Likely Democrat to Lean Democrat, as Republican Christine Drazan mounts a close rematch against Democratic Gov. Tina Kotek. Recent public polls show the race within the margin of error.

Worries about homelessness, housing, taxes, schools and the cost of living have opened a door for Republicans in a state where they haven't won the governorship in more than four decades. Drazan lost to Kotek by less than four points in 2022, then went back to the legislature, where she served again as House minority leader before being appointed to the state Senate.

Drazan is keeping her campaign focused on local problems and on ending one-party rule. "Oregon needs change," she told Fox News Digital, adding that single-party control "has not been good for us." She also said the Republican Governors Association is now investing in her race.

Kotek's campaign is trying to tie Drazan to Trump, who is unpopular in Oregon, and the Democratic Governors Association insists Kotek has the advantage. Drazan acknowledged that Kotek has a big fundraising lead, though Oregon's lack of contribution limits lets her compete.

Why it matters: Kamala Harris won Oregon by 14 points in 2024, so a competitive governor's race there shows how frustrated voters are with Democratic leadership, even in a year Fox describes as tough for Republicans nationally.

stories.headline: Drag queens, trans pastor, abortion rallies: Inside Dem governor hopeful's progressive church
stories.note: Iowa Democrat Rob Sand runs as a faith-driven moderate, but Fox reports his Des Moines church has hosted drag performers, a transgender guest pastor and abortion rallies.
body: Rob Sand, Iowa's state auditor and the Democratic nominee for governor, has built his campaign around his Christian faith and an independent, moderate image, even saying he has voted for Republicans and calling political parties "poison."

But Fox News Digital reports that, as of late 2025, Sand regularly attended Plymouth Congregational United Church of Christ in Des Moines, according to a local journalist. The church describes itself as LGBTQ+ affirming for more than 30 years, says it doesn't read the Bible literally, and is called "a progressive powerhouse" in a United Church of Christ profile.

Fox found the church hosted drag performer Flamy Grant for a concert in 2025, promoted a drag karaoke fundraiser, and had transgender pastor Paula Stone Williams as a guest pastor in 2023. It also offers a sexuality education program starting in first grade, held a vigil supporting abortion in 2022, rallied against abortion limits in 2023, and its pastors joined a 2025 statehouse protest backing transgender Iowans.

Sand's campaign said he attends church weekly, has never found a church he agrees with on everything, and prefers traditional services. It also attacked GOP nominee Zach Lahn over a past investment in a sexual wellness device company and his trips to Kansas, which Lahn says are to bring his children back and forth.

Why it matters: The Lahn campaign argues the church shows Sand's real values don't match Iowa's. In one of the country's most closely watched governor's races, anything that cracks Sand's moderate image is a big opening for Republicans.

stories.headline: EXCLUSIVE: Inside LA's homeless hellscape — unlikely critics blast Dems as GOP hopeful tours Skid Row
stories.note: GOP governor candidate Steve Hilton toured Skid Row and called California's homelessness a 'political scandal,' while even locals who voted Democrat blasted Mayor Karen Bass.
body: Republican governor candidate Steve Hilton walked through Los Angeles' Skid Row with Fox News Digital and blamed years of Democratic leadership for the encampments, open drug use and filth there, calling homelessness "a political scandal" rather than a crisis no one could prevent.

The tour came days after a sweeping federal and local drug raid in the neighborhood, in which the FBI, DEA and LAPD arrested 23 of 28 people charged with dealing fentanyl, meth and other drugs. In September, federal prosecutors also charged the founder of an LA homelessness nonprofit that received more than $118 million in public money with wire fraud, alleging he spent nearly $50,000 of it on a trip to Tahiti.

Hilton argued that politically connected developers and taxpayer-funded nonprofits profit from the problem, and said his plan starts with enforcing the law and getting people off the streets. He also hit Democratic opponent Xavier Becerra for skipping debates and taking voters for granted.

Criticism came from unexpected places. A Skid Row food volunteer named Venus said she had voted for Bass but that the mayor "lied about the homeless" and did nothing to fix it. A man who called himself a member of the American Communist Party said California's leaders aren't doing nearly enough.

Why it matters: With voting already underway in the Nov. 3 race, homelessness and billions in spending are once again a top issue, and Hilton is betting fed-up Californians are ready to give a Republican a chance.

stories.headline: SC Dem Senate candidate claims she will stand up to her party as Graham ties her to 'socialist Democrats'
stories.note: In Sunday's South Carolina Senate debate, Trump-backed Sen. Darline Graham warned Democrat Annie Andrews would side with 'socialist Democrats' rather than stand up to them.
body: Sen. Darline Graham, the South Carolina Republican, faced Democratic challenger Annie Andrews and Libertarian Kasie Whitener in a Senate debate Sunday night.

Graham said she is worried about "the socialist Democrats," pointing to Democrats in New York she said cheered after Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel. She told voters Andrews won't stand up to that wing of the party and is "only going to join them."

Andrews answered that Graham was reading from a script meant to tie her to Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and insisted she would stand up to her own party. She also took a jab at Graham's name, implying she had changed it recently.

Graham responded that her legal name has always been Graham, explaining that she kept it after losing her parents as a young girl so she would feel connected to them. Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her to finish the term of her late brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham, and Trump is backing her for a full six-year term.

Why it matters: Fox Power Rankings recently moved South Carolina from Solid to Likely Republican, and Graham's debate message, tying her opponent to the party's far left, is the GOP's main argument for holding the seat.
